Painter Norman Rockwell choreographing the photograph he based his painting "First Trip to the Beauty Shop" on. Massachusetts. 1972

Norman Rockwell (February 3, 1894 – November 8, 1978) was a 20th-century American author, painter and illustrator. His works enjoy a broad popular appeal in the United States for their reflection of American culture. Rockwell is most famous for the cover illustrations of everyday life he created for The Saturday Evening Post magazine over nearly five decades.

To prepare for his paintings, he first brought his ideas to life in a photography studio by staging scenes that are fully realized works of art in their own right. Using various photographers, he selected props and locations and choose and directed his models to carefully orchestrate each element of his design for the camera before beginning to paint.

The finished painting may be seen here.

Several more examples of the process may be seen here.
He did the majority of covers for the Saturday Evening Post for most of the 20th Century.
